name: Ossek Tamarind-Pomelo
description: A tart, complex soda that layers real pomelo extract over a synth-tamarind base — one of the few Ossek products that uses any real ingredient, which they use as a quiet selling point on the label.
flavor_profile: Sharp citrus bitterness from pomelo, deep sour-sweet tamarind body, mild sweetness, dry and complex finish
cultural_context: Ossek has a reputation for no-nonsense branding in a category full of lifestyle marketing. Their half-real, half-synth positioning resonates with Tier 2 consumers who are skeptical of both luxury pretension and bottom-shelf quality. The label just lists ingredients — no imagery, no gradient.
story_hooks: Ossek's pomelo supplier — a small licensed greenhouse operation outside the city corridor — has just been bought by a corponation. Ossek has two months before their 'real extract' claim becomes a lie.
A food critic with a BCI-integrated palate has publicly ranked Ossek Tamarind-Pomelo above several Tier 4 premium sodas. The backlash from those brands has been disproportionate.
Someone has been counterfeiting Ossek cans — the fake product is actually higher quality than the real one, which raises uncomfortable questions about who's behind it and why.
